title: Reverse One Stretch of a Chain
statement:
You get the head of a singly linked list and two positions left ≤ right, counted from 1. Reverse the order of the nodes from position left to position right, keep everything else in place, and return the head of the resulting list.

Try to do it in one pass, rewiring the existing nodes.

examples.why: Positions 2 to 4 hold 20, 30, 40. They flip; 10 and 50 stay where they are.
The stretch starts at the head, so the head itself changes. A dummy node in front avoids a special case.
A stretch of one node reversed is the same node.

hints: First walk to the node just before position left. What should happen if left is 1 and there is no such node?
Put a dummy node in front of the head. Then "the node before the stretch" always exists.
From there, repeat right − left times: take the node right after the stretch's current first node and move it to the front of the stretch (just after the node before).

explain.intuition:
Reversing a whole list is easy; the hard part here is stitching the reversed piece back in at both ends. A dummy node in front of the head turns "the node before position left" into something that always exists, even when left = 1.

Then use front insertion. Let prev be the node before the stretch and cur the stretch's first node. cur will end up last in the stretch, so it never moves. Each step, unhook the node right after cur and insert it right after prev. After right − left such moves the stretch is reversed and both ends are already connected.
steps: Create dummy with dummy.next = head. Walk prev forward left − 1 times from dummy.
Let cur = prev.next, the first node of the stretch.
Repeat right − left times: move = cur.next; cur.next = move.next; move.next = prev.next; prev.next = move.
pitfalls: Returning head instead of dummy.next. When left = 1, the old head is no longer first.
Losing the rest of the list: if the last stretch node is not reconnected to the node after right, the tail disappears.
Counting positions from 0. The positions here start at 1.

solutions.title: Copy values, reverse the slice
solutions.idea: Read the values into an array, reverse the slice from left − 1 to right − 1, and write the values back into the nodes.

solutions.title: Dummy node + front insertion
solutions.idea: Find the node before the stretch. Repeatedly move the node after the stretch's first node to the front of the stretch.

followups: Reverse every block of k nodes in the list. Which part of this solution can you reuse?
Do it recursively. What does the recursion stack cost?
